findings.title: still present since round 1 (B2, regressed): delta-0 activate is a NO-OP on the palette + scale rows — touch row-taps, mouse row-clicks, keyboard Enter and pad A can never change them
findings.detail: settings_click calls effect_settings_adjust(..., 0); Enter and pad A emit Settings_Activate{delta=0}; exec passes v.delta through; cycle_scale/cycle_palette(cur,0)==cur (pinned by the shipped test 'a zero delta holds the step'). Touch has NO +/- gesture, so a touch-only player cannot change palette or UI scale AT ALL — worse than r1's one-way ratchet. The PR claim 'a touch-only player can always get back (150% -> 100% on the next tap)' is false as shipped, as is the in-code comment 'a delta-0 tap advances'.
findings.evidence: main.odin:796 'effect_settings_adjust(app.input.user, &app.input, i32(row), 0)' | mouse.odin 'case .Enter: append(out, Intent(Settings_Activate{delta = 0}))' | controller.odin:47 'case .A: append(out, Intent(Settings_Activate{delta = 0}))' | exec.odin:72 'inp.on_settings_adjust(inp.user, inp, inp.panel_row, v.delta)' | settings.odin:150-151 'cycle_scale :: proc(cur: u8, delta: i32) -> u8 { n := i32(UI_SCALE_COUNT); return u8((i32(cur) + delta + n) % n) }' | probe test: both expects FAILED (step/mode unchanged)
findings.recommended_fix: Normalize delta 0 -> +1 for the cycle rows at the adjust site (e.g. d := delta == 0 ? 1 : delta in effect_settings_adjust), or make cycle_*(cur,0) advance. Add the tap-path pin (a settings_click/adjust test asserting the step changes) — the shipped tests pin the no-op.

findings.title: QoS manual editor (r2 rework): weight values render INSIDE the [−] buttons and lane labels drift off their buttons at ×1.25/×1.50 — the B5 fix scaled the hit rects but left the draw loop raw
findings.detail: The manual-editor draw loop keeps raw 'x := QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane * 96' and draws the weight value at raw x+44 with raw font 14, while the nudge rects scale through hud(). At ×1.25 the minus rect spans 50..75 and the value draws at 64 — inside it; at ×1.50 the value sits inside 60..90. Lane 1/2 values land on/near the PREVIOUS lane's [+] (138..168 at ×1.50). E9.3 'chrome stays legible at each step' fails on the exact surface B5 reworked.
findings.evidence: qos_panel.odin:351 'x := QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane * 96' | :361 'draw_text(app, wv, i32(x + 44), y + 4, 14, p.ink)' | vs qos_nudge_rect: 'x := rnd.hud(&app.view, QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane * 96)' + rects at x+hud(20)/x+hud(72), hud_f sizes
findings.recommended_fix: Route the draw loop through the same scaled math as qos_nudge_rect (derive label/value x from the rects: value centered between minus.x+width and plus.x; labels hud-scaled; font hud(14)).

findings.title: linear_to_srgb is mathematically wrong in BOTH the committed derivation script and the palcheck simulator — divides instead of multiplies and branches at the forward threshold
findings.detail: linear_to_srgb uses 'c / 12.92 if c <= 0.04045'; the correct inverse is 'c * 12.92 if c <= 0.0031308 else 1.055*c^(1/2.4) − 0.055'. Dark linear outputs crush to ~0 instead of their true sRGB values (linear 0.02 -> 0 instead of 43). The derivation record does NOT implement the claimed 'sRGB→linear→matrix→back' Machado simulation, and the oracle measures separation in the same wrong space — the pinned min sim-dists (51.3/54.7/43.0) and the CI separation guarantee are computed under a broken codec.
findings.evidence: derive_a11y_palettes.py:40 'v = c / 12.92 if c <= 0.04045 else 1.055 * (c ** (1 / 2.4)) - 0.055' | palcheck.odin:45 'v := c / 12.92 if c <= 0.04045 else 1.055 * math.pow(c, 1.0 / 2.4) - 0.055' | cvd_simulate (the oracle's simulator) calls it
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the inverse pair in BOTH files (multiply + 0.0031308 threshold), re-verify separation under the corrected simulator, re-derive/re-tune the tables if any pair falls below threshold, re-bless goldens cause-documented if values change.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: FAIL

Overall ~78%. Fails on P0 and overall.

findings.title: QoS preset chips double-scale their x offset — the 3rd chip overflows the panel card +48px at ×1.25 and +126px at ×1.50
findings.detail: qos_preset_chip_rect computes chip width w in scaled space, then re-scales the whole offset: hud(QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + i*(w+4)) — the i*(w+4) term passes through hud twice. Exact math: at ×1.25 chips land at x 25/174/323 vs panel right 390 (3rd chip ends 438); at ×1.50 30/243/456 vs 468 (ends 594). Hit==draw (still clickable) but the chip renders outside the card over the map.
findings.evidence: qos_panel.odin:94 'w := (rnd.hud(&app.view, QOS_PANEL_W) - rnd.hud(&app.view, 16) - rnd.hud(&app.view, 4) * (n - 1)) / n' | :95 'return {f32(rnd.hud(&app.view, QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + i * (w + 4))), ...'
findings.recommended_fix: Compute x incrementally in scaled space (x := hud(base); per chip x += w + hud(4)) — never feed a scaled quantity back through hud().

findings.title: QoS draw-side leftovers: the lane proportion bar (raw x/y/h + raw width math) collides with the scaled lane label at ×1.25+, and the queue-depth label stays unscaled
findings.detail: The lane label draws at hud(QOS_PANEL_X+10) with hud(15) font, but the proportion bar is rl.DrawRectangle(QOS_PANEL_X + 118, y + 7, bw, 8) raw — at ×1.50 the ~22px label text reaches ~165px and the bar starts at raw 130 (overlap). The queue-depth label (QOS_PANEL_X+10, font 14 raw) likewise stays unscaled while its row scales.
findings.evidence: qos_panel.odin:313 'rl.DrawRectangle(QOS_PANEL_X + 118, y + 7, bw, 8, cols[lane])' | :375 'draw_text(app, depth_label, QOS_PANEL_X + 10, qd_y + 3, 14, p.ink_soft)'
findings.recommended_fix: hud()/hud_f() the bar rect, its width math, and the queue-depth label position/size.

findings.title: S is a dead key while the panel is open with a pipe selected (opened via chip tap or pad Y) — the footer 'S / tap chip to close' is false in that state
findings.detail: S is collected only when sel_pipe < 0. The chip and pad Y open the panel regardless of selection, so with a pipe selected the keyboard S neither closes the panel nor (correctly) fires a lane — it does nothing. Esc/Y/B/chip still close, so the panel is never trapped, but the advertised close key is dead in a reachable state.
findings.evidence: mouse.odin:103-104 'if inp.sel_pipe < 0 { if keys_n < len(keys) { keys[keys_n] = .S; ...' | settings_panel.odin:121 'draw_text_c(v, "S / tap chip to close", ...)'
findings.recommended_fix: Collect S for panel-close whenever panel_open (the ownership conflict only exists on the open side), or fix the footer text.

findings.title: Settings hit-test semantics now live in THREE hand-synced copies (app settings_click, parity_settings_press_effect, and the documented single-source rule) — the parity twin cannot see app-side adjust effects
findings.detail: The parity twin re-implements chip/row hit-testing instead of sharing settings_click, and models NO adjust. This is exactly the blind spot that let the delta-0 no-op (blocker 1) ship CI-green: the parity scenario asserts only input state. Any future divergence between the twin and the app path passes parity.
findings.evidence: parity.odin:140-160 parity_settings_press_effect duplicates the chip/row rect loops; comments in both files claim 'the same rects the app hit-tests' by hand-sync
findings.recommended_fix: Extract the hit-test into a shared proc (input-state-only core both call), or at minimum add an exec-level adjust assert so parity can fail on a dead adjust path.

findings.title: Harness capture computes crisis banner_y from RAW constants while the app hud-scales it — the ×1.50 blessed golden under-pins the app's banner placement
findings.detail: capture_frame uses banner_y = 10 / 10+HEALTH_CARD_H+6 raw; the app's banner_y() returns hud(...) of the same expression.
